Commentary.Commentary: Roland-Jones is having a debut to remember so far. A five-for to follow up his exploits with the bat leaves the African side playing the catch up game after one innings of both sides. Apart from him, Anderson chipped in with three wickets. Stay with us, as the home team openers will walk out to face the visiting bowlers in their second innings.

A late order decent batting saw the South Africans finish 178 runs adrift of the first innings score of England. Bavuma is the man who led the fightback for the visitors. He scored a steady half century before being the last man to fall. He stitched up useful stands, first with Rabada and then with Morkel to propel the away side.

OUT! Take a bow, Roland-Jones! Gets a five-wicket haul on his Test debut. What a beginning to his career in the longest format of the game. He steams in and bowls a length delivery outside off. Gets it to come in with the angle. Bavuma plants his front foot across and feels that he has it covered. However, the ball nips away after pitching and that induces a faint outside edge. Bairstow moves to his right and pouches it nicely. An enterprising knock from Temba comes to an end. SOUTH AFRICA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 175!
Short delivery outside off, Philander looks to cut it initially but ends up getting a top edge over extra cover for a single. He was not in control of that shot.
This one takes off! On a length outside off, Philander plants his front foot across and leaves it.

FOUR! In the air... but safe! Good length delivery outside off, Philander hops and pokes at it but gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies past the diving Jennings at third slip and goes through to the boundary.
Fullish delivery outside off, tapped to short cover.
That's a peach! On a length and it comes in with the angle initially. After pitching, it seams away. Bavuma does well not to follow it. Keeps his bat inside the line to evade it.
On a length outside off, played with an open face to backward point.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Good length delivery angling into Philander. He is hurried by it, hops back and looks to tuck it but is struck on the thigh pad. His bottom hand came off while playing that.
FOUR! Philander gets off the mark in style! Fractionally overpitched around off, Vernon leans ahead and dives it past the diving mid off fielder to find the fence.

The first hour of play is done and it's time for Drinks. Even though England have sent Morkel back to to the dressing room, the South Africans have scored runs, and importantly have avoided the follow-on. Bavuma is batting past his half century with an able batter in Philander for company.
Full length delivery outside off, swinging in a touch. Temba covers his off stump and sees it through safely.
Gets this one to curve back into Bavuma. He covers the line and pushes it down the track.
This time Temba with an angled blade taps it to the off side.
Fuller in length around off, played with soft hands to covers.
On a length outside off, Bavuma lets it go.
8th Test fifty for Temba Bavuma.

FOUR! Streaky way to reach his half century! Length delivery around off, Bavuma feels for it and gets a thick outside edge. It goes past the second slip fielder and through to the third man fence. It has been a fighting knock from the Protea middle order batsman. He will look to add some handy runs more.
Toby Roland-Jones to have a burst again.
Similar length delivery, pushed to covers.
Full length ball, driven to mid on.
Fullish delivery, Philander comes half-forward and defends it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish delivery on middle and leg, defended off the inner half of the bat.
Vernon Philander does walk in to bat. He spent the night in the hospital, and after lots of speculation  about whether he would be fit to bat, here he is, the last man walking out to bat!

Mike Atherton talks on air about his discussion with Kevin Pietersen about batting techniques. KP believes that getting the head to the ball rather than the feet to the ball, as most experts say, is the key and a better technique. Temba Bavuma's crack in the previous over drove home the point in plenty.

OUT! Anderson strikes! The stubborn 47-run stand and a gritty knock from the southpaw comes to an end! James steams in and bowls a good length delivery on middle. Morkel is tentative in his approach as he hangs back. After landing, the ball seams away substantially. The southpaw hangs his bat to counter it but ends up getting a thick outside edge. Alastair Cook at first slip has got bucket like hands. He moves to his right and takes a nice reverse cup catch.
Quicker delivery this time, Temba does well to defend it.
Shorter in length, pushed off the back foot to covers.
Looks to play it with the spin but it is not there. Gets it off the outer half to point.
A bit flatter this time on off, played with an open face towards point.
Floated around off, played with soft hands to covers.
Fullish delivery, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish outside off, shaping away. Left alone. End of a testing over.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
That was a peach! Anderson hits the deck hard and angles it in initially. After pitching, it seams away to go past the hanging bat of Bavuma. He didn't have any clue about that.
Nipping in from a length outside off, Bavuma knows where his off stump is and lets it go.
FOUR! Beautiful! Full delivery outside off, Bavuma drives it crisply through covers for an exquisite boundary. Moves to 48 with that. He is well set now.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Jimmy Anderson into the attack for the first time today.

Morkel survives! Going down the leg side, Morkel looks to clip it but it seems to have taken his pad on its way and into Bairstow's gloves. The wicket keeper appeals and looks confident. However, Ali tells him there was no bat involved. The replays confirm so.
Tossed up delivery, defended off the front foot.
Ali is threatening to break this partnership! This one again comes in with the arm. Morkel stays back and gets an inside edge onto his pads which saves him.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Almost a wicket! Another arm ball around off, Morkel prods forward to defend but the ball skids on to just go past the off stump.

Loud shout for an LBW denied! Ali comes around the wicket and bowls a slider. It comes in with the arm. Morkel looks to defend it but it goes past his defense. He is pinged on the front pad and the English side appeal confidently. However, it is turned down. Root has a look at Moeen but doesn't take the review. It was clearly going down leg.
Time for spin now. Moeen Ali comes into the attack. Can he break this blossoming partnership?
Fullish delivery swinging in on this occasion. Turned to mid-wicket.
Full length ball outside off, swinging away a touch. Bavuma makes a watchful leave.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

FOUR! SA avoid the follow-on! Their entire camp will be relieved. Fullish delivery outside off, Bavuma leans ahead a touch and drives it with an open face through cover-point. High elbow in that stroke and the timing was sublime. He picks up another boundary to his name.
Fuller length ball outside off, Temba doesn't fiddle with it.
On a length outside off, tapped to covers.
Leg stump line, tucked nicely through backward square leg. Ali hares to his left and cuts it off. However, Bavuma denies to take any run. That was strange. Two runs were there on offer.
Targeting the hips with a back of a length delivery, kept out watchfully.
Back of a length delivery slanting across Morne. Placed to point.
Deep square leg in place now and third slip moves to short mid-wicket. Could be a plan to bounce him out, or could be a bluff for the tailender.
Fullish delivery in line of the stumps, driven hard but straight to the man at mid on.

FOUR! Morkel is taking  the bowler on. Shortish delivery on middle, Morkel clears his front leg and drags it through the gap between mid on and mid-wicket. Has hit it decently and the ball rolls to the fence. SA need 2 more to avoid the follow-on.
Fullish delivery, driven to mid on.

DROPPED! It was a tough chance though. Fuller length ball outside off, this time Bavuma gets lured into an expansive drive. He goes at it with hard hands but gets a thick outside edge towards gully. It is traveling at a fast pace towards Stokes who is stationed there. He dives full length to his left and tries to take it one-handed but the ball pops out of his hand. He is disappointed.
Fullish delivery well outside off, swinging away. Bavuma lets it go on its way.
Bavuma shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot to gully.
Leg bye! Straying on the hips, Morkel looks to tuck it but the ball brushes his thigh pad and rolls through backward square leg. A leg bye taken.
Short of a length on middle, defended solidly off the back foot.

FOUR BYES! Back of a length delivery on middle, angles down the leg side sharply. Bairstow moves to his right, dives but has no chance to stop it. The ball rolls to the fine leg fence. Four byes signaled by the umpire.
Today is CRICKET UNITED DAY, due to which the stumps are blue in colour. It is a charity idea, the proceeds of which will be used for cricket beneficiaries.
Outside off and Bavuma doesn't bother to play at it. Six leaves in a row and that's a maiden.
On a length outside off, no movement whatsoever. Temba remains circumspect in approach as he leaves it alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
In the zone outside off, third leave in a row.
Well bowled! Hurls this one fuller around off and swings it away. Bavuma resists the temptation to drive as he plants his front foot across.
Back of a length outside off, holding its line. Bavuma points his bat skywards to allow it through.

FOUR! Morkel is having a bit of fun! Length delivery around off, Morkel swings across the line and ends up dragging it towards mid on. Anderson dives to his left but has no chance to stop it. A boundary results. SA need 11 more to avoid the follow-on.
Good length delivery in line of the stumps, Morne remains composed in defense.
Broad comes from over the wicket and bowls a length delivery on off, Morkel answers it with a straight bat.
Short and width on offer, cut away through point for a brace.
Good length delivery angling into Morkel. He hops back and looks to keep it out but is struck on the thigh pad. Broad is looking to bring the forward short leg into play.
On a fuller length wide outside off, Morkel with minimal feet movement swings at it wildly. Misses it altogether. It was similar to the way he got beaten to Broad some time ago.
Leg stump line this time, clipped straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Half-volley outside off, Temba drives it sweetly to mid off. Broad stationed there moves to his right and bends low to stop it.
Back of a length on off, Temba is assured with himself as he defends it stoutly beside the pitch on the leg side.
Loose shot! Short of a length delivery outside off, Bavuma plays at it away from his body with minimal feet movement and gets beaten.
Bavuma is having an issue with the bat and he discusses it with the umpire. Signals for a replacement.
Fullish delivery angling in from outside off, Bavuma goes for a booming drive but mistimes it back to Roland-Jones.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for SA! Fractionally overpitched just outside off, Temba drives it confidently past the bowler. It races through the mid on region and reaches the fence. The Proteas only need 17 more runs to avoid the follow-on.

FOUR! Crisp! Fullish delivery outside off, Morkel leans into it and caresses it through extra cover. The timing is spot on and the ball whistles away to the fence. Perhaps Bavuma needs to trust Morne more.
Fullish in length and tailing into Temba. He works it through backward square leg. Decides to take the single this time. He gets to 1000 RUNS IN TEST CRICKET with that run.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Full length ball outside off, driven sweetly to mid off.
Broad goes wide of the crease and angles this one sharply. Temba covers the line and blocks it down the track.
On a drivable length outside off, Bavuma resists the temptation and lets it go through to the keeper.
There's a mini conference going between Broad, Root and Stokes. Probably a plan to somehow bowl more to Morkel than Bavuma and end the innings sooner than later.

Fuller length ball outside off, Bavuma goes at it with hard hands but gets it off the outer half behind point. The fielder hares after it and stops it near the fence. Bavuma only takes a run. He wants to keep the strike as much as possible.
Bavuma shuffles across to the fullish delivery outside off and taps it to mid on.
Roland-Jones keeps it full outside off in search of some swing. It does shape away a little but it is wide enough to leave.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven to extra cover.
In the channel outside off, Bavuma plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Full ball outside off, driven towards Ali at covers who makes a nice half-stop to parry it towards cover-point. There is  a single on offer but he decides not to take it.
The hero of yesterday, Toby Roland-Jones to bowl from the other end. Two slips and a gully in place.
Full length delivery wide outside off, swings away after pitching. Morkel goes for an expansive drive but gets beaten.
Fullish delivery in line of the stumps, wristed towards mid-wicket.
Broad tries to tuck Morkel up with a shortish delivery. The southpaw hops and looks to fend it off but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Fuller length delivery on off, Morkel opts to stay back and blocks it.
Short of a length delivery around off, Morne is opened up a bit in his stance as he gets it off the outer half to Ali at backward point.
Sprays this one down the leg side, Morkel looks to glance it but misses.
No ball! False start from Broad as he oversteps! Full length delivery on middle and leg, Morkel tucks it towards wide mid on.
The men who matter are out in the middle. Stuart Broad to bowl first up with a short leg in place. Morne Morkel on strike, Temba Bavuma at the other end.

Greetings for the day, fellas, wherever you are! Welcome to the coverage of the third day's play between England and South Africa. The news is that Vernon Philander is available to bat for the visitors. England will be pondering over whether to enforce the follow-on or not, if such a scenario arises. Stay with us for the rest of what could be a decisive day in this Test, as we bring you all the action from The Oval.
... DAY THREE, SESSION ONE ...

Amidst the dark clouds hovering above, Temba Bavuma was the silver lining for the visitors. He saw off the danger period through and then gutsed it down to stay unbeaten at the end of the day. He will be hoping to take his team past the follow-on mark tomorrow and gain some sort of respectability. Do join us at 1100 local (1000 GMT) for all the action from Day 3 of this third Eng-SA Test. In the meanwhile, you can also catch all the action from the ongoing Sri Lanka-India Test at Galle. Adios! Take Care!

Follow-on or not? One of the most irritating questions fielding captains have to face. South Africa need another 28 to avoid that and if they get that tomorrow, the choice will go out of Joe Root's hands. South Africa lost Philander today due to a mystery illness and he is recovering in the hospital but the news from the camp is that he might just come out tomorrow to bat. Do not bet against South Africa trying that.

England bowled well as a unit. The conditions were suited to their bowlers with the dark clouds showing full loyalty, aiding massive movement. Hard to point out much faults in the South African batting, so good was the bowling.

After his run-a-ball 25 with the bat earlier on, Roland-Jones came in running pretty innocuously to bowl his first ball. Within a matter of 30 minutes, he had Elgar, Kuhn, Amla and de Kock in the hut. South Africa's backbone was being cut into two but there was more misery to come. They slipped to 61/7 before a 53-run stand between Bavuma and Rabada saved them an embarrassment of being bowled out under 100 for the 5th time since re-admission in Tests.

When you see so many wickets in a session, you normally attribute to the experienced guys - the Jimmys or the Broadys. But nay, it was a 29-year old lad from Middlesex, TOBY ROLAND-JONES, who just made the evening his own. Or perhaps, more than just an evening. It was his day to remember.

End of a lonnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnng yet entertaining session. 108/7 in 34.2 overs. Do we need to say who bossed it? How have the tables turned! Just yesterday, we were thinking, that England are not in a good position and were saved by the rain. Come Friday, the hosts have just catapulted to the top.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended. STUMPS ON DAY 2, SOUTH AFRICA TRAIL BY 227!
Shorter and outside off, punched through the covers and this time he gets a couple. 28 more needed to avoid the follow-on.

Full and wide outside off, Temba leans and pushes it through the covers. He initially sets off for the single thinking he will get two but then realizes that there is only one available, so sends Morkel back.
The field now comes in, denying Bavuma the single.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler who deliberately allows it go to long on, teasing Bavuma to take the run but he doesn't move.
Landed outside off, Bavuma strides forward and then lets it go.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.

The light has dimmed in and Aleem Dar has a look at the light meter. We just have time for one more over and Toby Roland-Jones will not bowl it. MOEEN ALI to bowl the final over of the day. Keaton Jennings comes under the lid at short leg.
Outside off, moving away, left alone comfortably.
Full and straight, MM chips it uppishly wide of mid on.
Works this straight to short mid-wicket.
Good length ball, around middle and leg, Morne hops and pushes it to the leg side.

Huge appeal for LBW, turned down. As always, Broad wants a review. Bairstow convinces Root to go against his wish. Rightly so. This came in a long way from around the wicket, beat Morkel's defense and pinged him on the pad. Going down leg.
On a length outside off, steep bounce, even the 'Giraffe' has to hop to fend the ball. It dies down on the off side.

Another brilliant leave to finish the over. Trusts the ball coming in with the angle and then lets it go with his judgement. The cherry does not miss the off stump by much but Bavuma seemed to know where the stump was.
Full and outside off, Bavuma comes forward and pushes it to the off side.
Down the leg side, TB tucks it towards fine leg but does not take the single.
This one comes in with the angle from well outside off, Temba lets it go again.
Okay. The clock ticks past 1850. Whatever happens now, the third innings will not start before tomorrow.
On a good length again, comes in from outside off, Bavuma shoulders arms and then it moves away from him to the keeper.
Around middle and off, punched through cover-point for a single. The deficit is now 229.

FOUR! Kind of edgy this time. On a good length outside off, Bavuma looks to fend it off the steep bounce and luckily for him, the ball goes off the outside edge onto the ground, past the slip cordon and into the third man fence.

FOUR! Interesting. Full and wide outside off, Bavuma, with nothing to lose, leans and lofts it cleanly over covers. Gives a nice pose for the photographers. Just wondering, had this come around 30 minutes earlier, the South African score would have been somewhere around the follow-on mark.
Down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a single.

MORNE MORKEL walks in at number 10, replacing Rabada. With Philander in the hospital, this could be the last wicket. If it falls in the next 4-5 minutes, one of the two teams will have to come out to bat for around 5-10 minutes.

OUT! BOWLED! The change of bowling works! Broad is all smiles. He targets Rabada from around the wicket, angles this in, Rabada looks to defend but then Broad gets it to move away off the deck. The batsman misses it altogether and the ball pegs the off stump back. End of a fine resistance.

Another edge, goes to ground. Broad bends his back and then extracts extra bounce. Rabada pokes at it but gets an outside edge. The ball dies down in front of gully where Ben Stokes dives to his right to stop it one-handed.
On a length outside off, left alone.
STUART BROAD comes back on, possibly for his final spell of the day. He has been warming up for the last 15 minutes or so.
On a good length outside off, shouldered arms to.
Another flick, another run.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
50-run stand is up! Some sort of a recovery this. They are still in a crisis but if this pair manages to see the team through tonight, it will be a moral victory.
FOUR! Another outside edge. This time it is Bavuma. He pokes at a length ball, only to get an outside edge past third slip to third man!
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Fortuitous. But Rabada won't mind. Full and outside off, moving away, Rabada looks to drive but the ball goes off the outside edge, along the ground past gully to third man!
Length ball on off, defended down the ground by Bavuma.
Back of a length on off and middle, Rabada plays it with soft hands on the leg side for a quick single.
Very full on leg, Rabada this time flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Very full ball on leg and angling down the leg side. Rabada misses the flick and falls over, as the ball rolls next to the pitch.
Length ball outside off, he again shoulders arms to that one.
Back of a length ball from around the wicket, Rabada lets the keeper collect the ball without disturbing it.
Length ball on leg, blocked by Bavuma.
Length ball on off, Rabada collects a single towards cover-point to BRING UP SOUTH AFRICA'S 100!
Length ball outside off, Rabada lets it go.
Back of length ball on off, punched off the back foot.
FOUR! Back of length ball outside off, Rabada tentatively pokes at that. The ball takes the toe end of the bat and goes through the slip cordon, into the third man fence for a boundary.
Full ball on off, drives it back to the bowler who half-stops it on his followthrough and parries it over to mid on.
Toby Roland-Jones, the star of the day with the ball, with figures of 8-3-22-4 to bowl now.
Fuller ball outside off, driven straight to point.
Shortish ball on off and middle, Bavuma flicks it towards mid on.
Back of length ball on off, defended to the off side..
Length ball outside off, Bavuma doesn't play that.
Fuller ball on middle and leg, he flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run. Bavuma wants the second and rightfully denied.
Length ball outside off, Stokes lets that go.
The umpires again brought out their light meters to measure the light. Strangely, they deem it fit for Stokes to ball, and he's into the attack now.
Blocks that loopy ball from the crease.
Slow ball outside off, cut away for a run.
Flighted on off, blocked back by Rabada.
Tossed up outside off, played towards point for a run.
Loopy ball on middle, driven through mid on for a single.
Flat and wide ball outside off, played towards deep point for a run.
Loopy ball played towards mid-wicket for no run.
Flights it on off, Rabada blocks that.
Flighted ball on middle, driven back to the bowler.
Tossed up on off, driven through mid off.
Floated on middle and off, driven to long on for a run.
Loopy ball outside off, driven through covers for a run.
Tossed up on middle, driven towards mid on for a quick single. Root fields that and has a shy at the bowler's end, but Rabada was in there.
Short and flatter on off, he cuts it to point.
Loopy ball on off, driven back to the bowler.
Flighted ball on leg and middle, it brushes Rabada's pads and runs down towards fine leg for a couple of leg byes.
Tossed up on off, Rabada bunts that down.
Full loopy ball outside off, Bavuma sweeps it towards fine leg to cross over.
Moeen Ali to bowl now and it's spin from both the ends.
Loopy ball on middle, driven down the ground by Rabada. Broad chased that from mid on and looped it to Anderson who came there from long off and returned it back to the bowler. They ran two.
Flighted full ball on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full toss on off, driven through mid on for a run.
That's a seam-up ball outside off, Bavuma doesn't fiddle with that.
Floated on off and middle, blocked off the front foot.
Starts off with a loopy low full toss on middle, driven back to the bowler.
Joe Root seems to introduce himself into the attack, as it seems that pacers can't bowl owing to the gloomy conditions.
The light meters are out and the visibility is being checked.
Length ball on off, defended by the batter.
Bouncer on middle, Rabada ducks under that.
Length ball on off, Rabada defends.

FOUR! STREAKY YET EFFECTIVE! Stokes steams in from round the wicket and bowls it a tad fuller on off, angling in to the batsman. Rabada closes the face of the bat to play it on the on side, but ends up getting a leading edge, that helps the ball race away though backward point and into the boundary fence. He wasn't in control, but South Africa won't mind the runs as long as they keep coming.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma picks up a single towards point.
Back of a length ball on off, played from within the crease.
Root is back on the field. Hopefully he is back with fresh ideas and tactics.
Full ball on off and middle, blocked solidly.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length ball on his pads, as he misses the flick he gets hit on the pads and they take a leg bye.
Fuller ball on off, he edges that towards the off side.
Length ball on off, it takes the inside edge of the bat.
Stokes is in charge at the moment. Root has gone out of the park for sometime. Could be a refreshment break or a nature's call given the climate there!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! A pleasant shot yielding runs after quite some time for the Proteas! That's pitched on off stump and is full in length. Rabada drives it through covers. Malan fielding at mid off chases and puts in the dive. He almost saves the boundary, but the momentum of the ball takes it in and after he slides into the fence, the ball hits the boundary cushion.
Back of a length ball on middle, Bavuma plays it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Length ball on off, Bavuma defends with an angled bat.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma guides it through point towards third man for a brace.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma points the bat upwards as he lets that go.
Full ball outside off, Rabada plays and misses.
That's a genuine edge that goes towards gully.
Another full ball outside off, Rabada goes for the drive and misses.
Back of a length ball on off, it strikes Rabada high on the pads.
Full ball outside off, he lets that go to the keeper.
Full ball outside off, it entices Rabada to drive and teases the outside edge.
Length ball outside off, he gets beaten.
That's a length ball on his pads, he flicks it away for a couple.

FOUR! He's standing tall among the fall! That was a back of a length ball outside off and even though he is a short man, he stands tall and punches it through the covers. The ball races away to the boundary.
Bavuma defends the length ball from the crease.
Full on middle and leg, Rabada flicks it on the leg side to open his account.
Kagiso Rabada is the next man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! That's catching practice for Alastair Cook. Back of a length ball outside off, Maharaj flays at that and gets a thick outside edge that flies to first slip. It flew to him at a comfortable height and he doesn't miss such dollies. He accepts that and the batsman walks back with a forlorn face. Stokes adds a wicket to his kitty to add to the century that he scored. South Africa in shambles.
Length on off, played towards point.
Bavuma points his bat skywards and lets that go.
Length ball on off, defended from the crease.
Good shot. That was a tad fuller outside off, Bavuma pushes it through mid off and takes a brace. Broad is the fielder on that occasion.
Length ball on off and middle, blocked by showing the full face of the bat.
Full ball on off, edged towards the slip cordon.
Length ball outside off, Maharaj shoulders arms to that one.
Length ball on off, defends it off the back foot.
That length ball takes the inside edge of the bat and hits his pads and rolls towards the off side. They take a run.
Bavuma shows no interest in playing that length ball outside off.
Length ball on off, defended from the crease.
NO BALL! Stokes oversteps. He bowls it down the leg side, where Bairstow only manages a half stop and concedes a bye.
Length ball outside off, Maharaj thinks of leaving that at the last moment. It takes the outside edge and rolls to the slip cordon.

FOUR OVERTHROWS! Anderson bowls it at a length on off, Maharaj plays it with soft hands towards mid-wicket and sets off for a run. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end and a wayward throw results in overthrows that races away to the boundary.
That's bowled on a length on off, Maharaj blocks it from the crease.
Length ball outside off, Maharaj fails to put bat on that.
Keshav Maharaj walks in next.

OUT! ANDERSON STRIKES! That's a fuller ball on off, enticing the drive from Morris. He does play that shot straight down the ground, only to give an easy catch back to Anderson. These are as easy as they come. The umpires check for the front foot, and it is really too close for comfort. The benefit of doubt goes in favour of the bowler and Morris' stay at the crease ends. South Africa are crumbling big time here.
Back of a length ball on off, Morris defends it from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, he plays that from within the crease. The ball takes the edge and rolls over to the slip cordon.
Fuller ball outside off moving in, Bavuma lets it go. Not a great over, but a maiden nevertheless.
Way too wide outside off to make him play there.
Back of a length ball outside off, Bavuma plays it with soft hands towards point.
Back of a length ball on off, extra bounce there, takes Bavuma's gloves and rolls towards the slip cordon.
Short ball wide outside off, Bavuma misses out on a boundary-hitting opportunity. He hits it straight to the fielder at point.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, Bavuma leaves it alone.
The dashing all-rounder Ben Stokes to have a bowl now.
That stayed low and Morris gets beaten all ends up. It was bowled on a good length outside off and it went on the bounce to the left of Bairstow.
Length ball defended by Morris.
Length ball on off, Morris bunts it town.
Good ball outside off, testing Morris. Length ball makes the batsman offer his bat and it teases the outside edge of the bat and lands in the keeper's gloves.
Wow! Well fielded by Anderson in his followthrough. That was bowled full on off, Morris drove it to the left of the bowler. JA stuck his left hand out and stopped it.
Full ball on middle and leg, Morris drives it with a straight bat to mid on.
Another leave by Bavuma to end the over.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma doesn't have anything to do with that.
A tad fuller outside off, Bavuma pokes his bat aimlessly at that.
Length ball on the stumps, Morris plays it towards mid-wicket and they sneak in a quick single. The substitute fielder has a shy at the stumps at the striker's end and misses.
Full ball driven back to the bowler.
Back of a length ball on off, Bavuma plays it with soft hands towards point and picks up a single.
He defends it off the front foot and into the ground.
Another beautiful length ball outside off, swinging away from the batsman. Morris plays and misses.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bowled on a driving length outside off, Morris swings his bat and the ball passes the edge of his bat.
Length ball on off, Morris blocks.
Full swinging ball outside off, Morris misses the ball.
Length ball on his pas, he misses the flick and they collect a leg bye.
That's unplayable! Back of length ball on off and coming in to him, Morris gets beaten on the inside in defense.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length ball on middle strikes him high on his pads.
Morris leaves that delivery outside off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another leave by Morris to the length ball outside off.
Morris off the mark by playing that length ball towards point.
Length ball outside off, played towards point.
Length ball outside off, Morris leaves.
Length ball on off, Morris blocks that.
Chris Morris walks in next.

OUT! Anderson strikes immediately! He joins the party now. It's a length ball on off that consumes du Plessis. The skipper shouldered arms to that one and the ball struck his back pad. On appealing, Joe Wilson the umpire rules him out. Du Plessis consults the non-striker and opts for a review. Ball tracker shows that it was clipping the top of off. So the onfield decision stays. Along with the skipper's wicket, their reviews are also exhausted. Half the Protea batsmen are back in the hut.
The Protea skipper is in trouble! He's been adjudged LBW. He has challenged that call...
Jimmy Anderson comes in for another spell.
Back of a length ball on off, Bavuma pokes his bat and edges that. The ball goes on the bounce to the third slip.
Length ball angling into the stumps, Bavuma lets it go as it is wide off the stumps.

BAVUMA BREATHES EASY! That was a back of a length ball on off and spearing into him. He tries to defend but the ball seems to have hit his pads and lobs to gully where Stokes dives and claims the catch. The umpire is not interested in any of the antics. Root deliberates over taking a review, but doesn't. Snicko shows a spike as the ball passes the bat. The ball fell short of the diving Stokes as seen from the replay.
The small man, Temba Bavuma walks in earlier than he would have loved.

OUT! ROLAND-JONES ON A ROLL AT THE OVAL! That's bowled on a good length on leg and middle, de Kock tries to flick that on the on side. All he manages is to get a leading edge and the ball picks out gully in precision. Stokes doesn't miss catches like these. TRJ gets his fourth. South Africa in deep deep trouble.
That's bowled full on off, de Kock times the drive through mid off. Anderson chases that valiantly, slides and keeps it down to two.
Du Plessis flicks that length ball off his pads for a single.
He does make him play now, keeping the ball around leg and de Kock defends it down the ground.
Five in a row. Broad needs to keep the line a bit around middle to make de Kock play.
Make that four leaves in a row now.
One more leave outside off as Broad gets it wider outside off.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Back of length ball outside off, du Plessis lets that go. 9 came off it.
Length ball on his pads, flicked away for a run.
FOUR! Now that's a shot where he is in command. Full on off, de Kock drives it on the up through mid off for another boundary. Roland-Jones just bowled that way too full.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Back of length ball on leg, hits de Kock on the pads as he misses it. The umpire declines the appeal. It sees to have pitched outside leg, and height too was a factor.

FOUR! Length ball on his pads, de Kock just nudges it fine. The ball races away to through the fine leg fence for a boundary. The umpire there seems to ask the batsman whether he had hit it or it went off his pads. Eventually it's given as runs in the batsman's kitty.
Solidly defended that from within the crease.
Length ball on off and middle, flicked away towards mid-wicket.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Length ball outside off, Faf lets it go.
Length ball on middle and leg, tucked away for a single.
FOUR! That's short and wide outside off, asking to be cut. De Kock obliges and cuts it in front of point. The ball races away to the boundary. That came right off the meat of the bat.
Skipper Francois du Plessis strides out, with his team in spot of bother.

OUT! TOBY ROLAND-JONES STRIKES FOR THE THIRD TIME! And it's the big fish Amla now! That's bowled back of a length just outside off, and it seams away after pitching. The batter has to hang out his bat and that's enough for the ball to take the batsman's glove and land safely in Bairstow's gloves. It's a really big wicket as Hashim is a grafter once he gets in. The Proteas lose three very quickly. England on top.
Full ball outside off, Amla drives that through covers. Moeen Ali chases it, slides and returns it back, before which they complete a brace.
Length ball on middle, Amla defends.
Length ball on middle and leg, flicked away on the leg side. Quinny gets off the mark with that.
STIFLED APPEAL by England there, as that back of length ball crashed into de Kock's pads. He missed the flick and the ball struck him high. The umpire stayed unmoved.
Full ball outside off, de Kock pushes it back to the bowler.
On a a length on off, Amla plays it off the back foot.
Length ball on off, Amla defends getting behind the line of the ball.
Well left ball outside off by Amla.
FOUR! Amla gets going with that glorious boundary. That's on a length outside off, he stretches forward and creams it through covers. It's so good that you can watch it again and again.
Another leave by Amla to a delivery outside off.
Length ball outside off, Amla lets Bairstow collect that one.
Full and down the leg side, de Kock ignores it. Bairstow doesn't collect cleanly and the ball could have hit his helmet lying behind.
Length ball outside off, he shoulders arms to that one.
A yorker on off and middle to welcome de Kock, which he digs out on the off side.
Quinton de Kock walks in at number 4.

OUT! What a debut Roland-Jones is having! He strikes second time in quick succession. That's bowled full on off from slightly wider of the crease, angling into the batsman. The length makes Kuhn go for a flick and he ends up missing the ball completely. The ball hits him on the back pad, which is adjacent to the stumps. This one's as plumb as it can get. They check for the no-ball, and the bowler is just fine there. Toby is on a roll, South Africa lose both their openers now.
Length ball outside off, Kuhn plays and misses that.
Full ball on off, Kuhn defends showing full face of the bat.
Length ball on middle, blocked from within the crease.
That's too wide to make him play there.
Amla shoulders arms to that ball outside off.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Length ball on middle, flicked away on the leg for a run.
FOUR! Shot! That was on a length outside off, Kuhn drives it beautifully through covers and the ball races away to the fence. He looked in complete control there.
Broad to continue from the other end.
Fuller ball outside off, Amla shoulders arms to that.

NOT OUT! And how close to a good review is that! That is bowled back of a length outside off and coming into Amla. That's a brilliant first ball to get. Amla prods forward in defense but misses the ball due to some late movement. England appeal for a very long time, the umpire after much deliberation stays unmoved. Root decides to review the call after discussing with his keeper and the bowler. The ball tracker returns that it just clipped the bails, and hence it is umpire's call and the onfield call stays. It isn't that bad a review, Amla survives to live another day!
Oh yes! England have reviewed a LBW call against Amla! More in optimism and the value of the player is what made them do so is what I reckon.
The weather has permitted resumption on time. Hashim Amla has walked out to bat. Roland-Jones will finish his over.
... DAY TWO, SESSION THREE ...

The persistent drizzle has spiced up the pitch to some extent. The ball has been moving around considerably and the English seamers are making full use of it. Toby Roland-Jones has been impressive in the little outing that he has had and he will now look to build on his maiden Test wicket. Join us at 1515 GMT (1615 local) to see how the final session unfolds. South Africa will hope they don't lose more than two wickets till close...

England will feel a lot more confident going into the break. Not that they were nervous, but a wicket just before the interruption will boost them. Elgar and Kuhn did very well to survive some tough calls but eventually Elgar has been consumed by one.

OUT! YES HE DEPARTS! And with him they lose a review. That is bowled full just outside off, inviting the drive. Almost instinctively, he pokes at that and as soon as Bairstow catches that, everybody apart from Roland-Jones appeal. The umpire rules him out, and if expressions do tell a tale, Roland-Jones' facial gestures suggest that he is surprised with that call. Elgar seeks to review that decision. The sniko shows a spike as the ball passes the bat. But since the bat and the pad were too close to each other, the spike could have been owing to the bat hitting the pads. This is where the absence of hotspot seems to hurt. The third umpire upholds the onfield call, and Elgar has to depart. What a way to get your first test wicket! Toby strikes, South Africa lose one, early in the piece. And that's TEA, DAY TWO!
Elgar has been adjudged caught behind! He has reviewed the decision almost immediately, suggesting that he didn't nick that.
Good length ball going across Elgar, he tentatively pokes his bat at it and the ball passes the edge of the bat.
Full ball just outside off, Elgar lets it go.
Back of length ball bowled over the wicket, Elgar defends it from within the crease.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Wide outside off, fuller in length, watchfully let through to the keeper.

SNORTER! Elgar is getting some good luck on his side. This is on a good length, outside off and Elgar pushes at it, half-forward. But out of nowhere, the ball kicks up, catches him by surprise and then beats the outside edge. As an opener and that too, in English conditions, Elgar must learn to forget such stuff. If you nick it, your bad luck. Else, forget the good ones and concentrate on the next ball.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Outside off again, let through.
Full and outside off, Elgar lets it through.
The batsman has stood up on his toes to play that one.
The rain is getting heavier...
Again, this is a plan to get him caught down the leg side. Kuhn walks across to flick, falls over in his attempt but misses the ball.
FOUR! That is a fine shot. Short and outside off, Kuhn gets on top of the bounce and cuts it in front of point for a boundary!

UPPISH, SAFE! Another close call. Elgar plays this aerially, away from his body and the ball nearly carries to point. It lands in front of the fielder who is unable to stop it and he parries it away, enabling the batsmen to take a single.
Slight drizzle in the air. It has become gloomy and the umbrellas are being taken out by the spectators.
This is wide outside off, let through.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
The debutant Toby Roland-Jones will be bowling earlier than we thought.
Another well left by Heino to a length ball outside off.
Kuhn has nothing to do with that harmless ball outside off.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

KUHN SURVIVES A CAUGHT BEHIND APPEAL! That is bowled on a good length on middle and angling down leg, he tries to flick. There's a noise as the ball passes the bat. Bairstow dives towards his left to grab that and England raise their appeal in unison. The umpire negates their appeal. Broad as always seems excited, yet England decide against reviewing that. Replays showed that the ball grazed his thigh pad on the way to the keeper, and that's what made the tickling sound.

FOUR! Wonderful use of the wrists by Kuhn. That was bowled on a good length on middle, he flicks it past the man at short leg and picks up a boundary. Ali ran in towards square leg but the ball raced to the fence before he could get there.
Length ball outside off, well left by Kuhn.
Root is having a short leg for Broad now. Tea at 1555 local time (1455 GMT). This session has been extended by 15 minutes.
Too wide of off to make him play there.
Length ball on off, elgar blocks showing full face of the bat.
Length ball on off and middle, he plays it with an angled bat towards third man. Stokes at gully puts in a dive and stops that.
Full and wide of off, Elgar lets that thud into Bairstow's gloves.
FOUR! Length ball starting on middle and leg, swinging down the leg side. Elgar got bat to that and flicked it away through fine leg for a boundary. Wasn't the greatest of deliveries by Anderson.
Good length ball on his pads, Kuhn flicks it towards backward square for a run.
Length ball outside off, Elgar plays and misses.

ALMOST! That was bowled full outside off, inviting the drive. Elgar accepts the invitation and goes for it. The ball just passes the outside edge of the bat and lands in the keeper's gloves. England almost had one there.
Elgar shoulders arms to the length ball outside off.
Elgar defends that ball bowled on a good length on middle.
Length ball outside off, Dean points his bat skywards and lets the keeper do the rest.
Fuller ball bowled around the wicket on middle and leg, Elgar tries to flick it and ends up getting a leading edge towards the bowler.
Length ball outside off, he lets that one go.
Fractionally full outside off, inviting the drive, Kuhn pushes it towards covers.
Fuller ball on off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, it strikes him high on the thigh pad and lobs on the leg side.
Length ball on middle, defended by Kuhn showing the full face of the bat.
Fuller ball on off, driven towards mid off.
A little hammering around where the bowler lands his front foot is being done, as Stuart Broad didn't seem happy with that area.
Full and down the leg side, Elgar tries to flick and misses.
Full ball on middle and leg, defended with a straight bat.
Fuller ball on off and middle, Elgar tries to play it on the leg side. He ends up getting a leading edge towards mid off.
Back of a length ball, Elgar covers the stumps and lets it go.
Well left by Elgar as that was bowled wide of off.
Round the wicket, he bowls it outside off, wide enough to let it go.
Stuart Broad runs in to bowl from the other end.
Fuller ball on middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
Length ball on leg, Elgar flicks that away.
Length ball on off, pushed through covers for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, he lets that go.
Full and that famous banana swing from Anderson on display as Kuhn leaves that full delivery outside off.
Starts of with a back of length ball on middle and off, Elgar plays it with soft hands from within the crease and takes off for a quick single. South Africa get going straightaway.
